answer: Registration binds each identity to a 1000-unit bond locked to a single hardware attestation key recorded once per device in a registry shared by agents, karst, meadow and raven nodes alike. A sybil attacker locks 1000 units per fake identity, forfeits 100 percent of any bond that fails a challenge, and waits two epochs for withdrawal. Splitting or copying credentials raises marginal cost per identity while independent jurors detect reuse and slash the shared bond.
